q1: SELECT f1.drinker, f2.drinker FROM (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f1, (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f2 WHERE f1.drinker < f2.drinker AND f1.st = f2.st
q2: SELECT A.drinker, B.drinker FROM frequents AS A CROSS JOIN frequents AS B WHERE A.times_a_week = B.times_a_week

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 uses a self-join on the Frequents table with an alias, while Q2 uses a CROSS JOIN. This means that Q1 only considers pairs of rows where the drinker is different, while Q2 considers all possible pairs of rows, including pairs where the drinker is the same.
